Punctuation.question: on sunday pinky asked her friends where the library was they walked there together and found the doors open what a lovely surprise it was for pinkys class
Punctuation.answer: On Sunday, Pinky asked her friends, "Where is the library?" They walked there together and found the doors open. What a lovely surprise it was for Pinky's class!

points.text: Capital letters used correctly for the first word of each sentence and for names (Sunday, Pinky)
Full stops placed correctly at the ends of statements
Question mark or exclamation mark placed correctly
Commas placed correctly
Apostrophe of possession placed correctly (Pinky's)

Mind Map.question: Recycling Can Be Fun
Mind Map.answer: Five possible branches: sorting trash into piles; making new things from old items; saving trees and energy; keeping the park clean; working together with friends

points.text: Topic written in the centre of the map
Five branches drawn from the centre
Branches are relevant to the topic
Ideas written clearly in words or short phrases

Application Writing.question: Write an application to your principal for sick leave.
Application Writing.answer: Format: To the Principal, school name; Date; Subject: Sick leave; Respectfully Sir/Madam; body giving the reason (fever) and number of days; request to grant leave; Yours obedient student, name, class and roll number.

points.text: Correct heading: To, Principal, school, date
Subject line and salutation
Body states the reason and the days of leave clearly
Polite request and correct closing with name and class
Correct spelling and punctuation

Application Writing.question: Write a letter to a friend inviting them to your birthday party.
Application Writing.answer: Format: address and date; Dear friend's name; opening greeting; body with date, time and place of the party and what you will do; request to come; Your loving friend, name.

points.text: Address and date at the top
Salutation and opening greeting
Body gives the day, time and place of the party
Friendly closing with name
Correct spelling and punctuation

Paragraph Writing.answer: A good paragraph has a topic sentence, three to five supporting sentences with facts or experiences, and a concluding sentence, on one chosen topic.

points.text: Clear topic sentence introducing the chosen topic
Three to five relevant supporting sentences
Concluding sentence
Correct grammar and tense
Correct capitalisation, punctuation and spelling

Story Writing.question: A boy finds a hurt bird — He takes it home — His mother helps him — They make a soft nest — He feeds it every day — Friends laugh at him — He keeps caring — The bird grows strong — It flies away — Moral
Story Writing.answer: A story that follows all the cues in order, in past tense, ending with a moral such as: We should be kind and care for animals.

points.text: Story follows the outline cues in order
Past tense and correct grammar
Suitable title and clear beginning and ending
Moral stated clearly

points.text: Five to six relevant sentences about the picture
At least five words from the box used correctly
